name: Stein Danielsen
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Solutions Officer, Cognite (per conference bio)
profile: Stein Hardy Danielsen co-founded Norwegian industrial data/AI software company Cognite in 2016 with John Markus Lervik and Geir Engdahl. Cognite's Cognite Data Fusion platform contextualizes industrial (oil & gas, energy, manufacturing) data; he has overseen applications and solutions built on it.
interesting_fact: Before Cognite he was Chief Architect at Cxense, and earlier CEO of Kopek; his background spans search, real-time systems, 3D graphics and large-scale data/transaction systems.
deep_cut_fact: He worked in product development at FAST (Fast Search & Transfer), the Norwegian enterprise-search company, and is also listed as a principal at Microsoft; he holds an MSc in Computer Science from NTNU.
notes: Low public profile; rarely interviewed. media@cognite.com seen in Dec 2025 Cognite HQ release (page blocked direct fetch; seen via search). Cognite is industrial/energy-data focused, a good podcast fit. Some sources spell his name 'Danielson'.

name: Charles Yeh
profile: Charles Yeh co-founded San Francisco identity-verification company Persona with CEO Rick Song in 2018 and serves as CTO. Persona raised a $200M Series D in April 2025 (led by Founders Fund and Ribbit) at a $2B valuation, positioning itself as a 'verified identity layer' for an agentic-AI world.
interesting_fact: Yeh tracks how fraudsters use generative AI: he notes deepfakes once carried detectable traces of their root models, but mixing models has made those traces harder to find. He is most interested in where identity and payments meet, especially privacy-conscious biometrics.
deep_cut_fact: Yeh was Rick Song's roommate for three to four years before Persona. He was the one who had long wanted to start a company and pushed Song to co-found one. Early on, he personally built a custom solution for a large Japanese identity-verification customer.
notes: Low profile compared with CEO Rick Song. No published press email found. Asked to describe founder life in one word, he chose 'Fulfilling' (Visa interview).

name: David Goate
profile: Software engineer David Goate co-founded London car insurer Marshmallow in 2017 with twins Alexander and Oliver Kent-Braham and is its CTO. It began by insuring migrants and expats who were overcharged by traditional insurers. It became a unicorn in 2021 with an $85M round at a $1.25B valuation, and later raised at a higher valuation.
interesting_fact: In 2018 the startup won a trademark battle against S&P 500 giant Marsh McLennan over the name 'Marshmallow', which the British press cast as David vs. Goliath. The FT ranked it Europe's 2nd-fastest-growing company in 2023 (660% CAGR).
deep_cut_fact: Goate and the Kent-Braham twins all previously worked at digital-identity company Yoti. The company was first incorporated in 2016 as 'Twin Thinking' and was renamed Marshmallow Technology in 2017, when the team went full time working from a gym (a Virgin Active lobby).
notes: Co-CEO twins are the public faces; Goate keeps a low profile. No published press email found (press page is JS-rendered). Sources for the gym and Twin Thinking details: Wikipedia and Yahoo Finance UK (au.finance.yahoo.com/news/entrepreneurs-tech-twins-behind-marshmallow-113830484.html).
